Six tests cover an object, null, a string, a number, an empty list and malformed JSON. Before this, a different shape would have thrown inside the loop over pull requests, outside its catch, as a stack trace on stderr with nothing on stdout.

This is the rule most at risk in a script that runs a command, and it holds. Every call uses execFileSync('gh', args) with the arguments as a list — ci-watch.mjs:22 and pre-merge-check.mjs:26 — so no shell is involved and nothing is interpolated into a command string. The two values that come from outside are both constrained before use: the pull request number is refused unless it matches digits only (pre-merge-check.mjs:21), and the job id is taken from a run URL by a digits-only capture (ci-watch.mjs:71) and discarded if absent. No eval, no new Function, and no shell: true anywhere in scope.

Nothing printed is a secret, token or personal datum: pull request numbers, titles, base branch names, check names, buckets and run URLs, all public in this public repository. No financial figure can reach the output, because the scripts never read the app's data, the seed or any export. The two error paths print one line of a message whose content, for a spawn or parse failure, is a command name and an errno or a shape complaint.

coverage.evidence: The input guard now has tests that attack it: ten cases in ci-scripts.test.mjs pass values shaped like a flag, a path traversal, a shell separator, a newline injection and a decimal, and each asserts both exit 2 and that the fake gh recorded no call, so nothing outside ever reached an argument list. SEC-30 holds independently, because gh is given a list and never a shell, so these prove the guard rather than being the only thing between the two. Recorded because it was not true earlier on this branch: the guard was correct by reading and had nothing attacking it, and could not be tested while the script ran at import. 093a231 made it importable and the ten cases were added.

summary: Pass, with 1 medium finding fixed and none open. No serious problem: SEC-30 holds — every gh call passes arguments as a list with no shell, and both outside values are digits-only before use, now with ten abuse tests proving the refusals never reach gh. SEC-06 checks gh's output shape as well. No secret, no personal data, nothing shipped to a device.
